name: List
summary: A vertical list of rows, each with a title and optional start, description, end, actions and a footer of buttons. Rows can be links or act in place, a row can hold one control across it, and a list can group its rows into sections with a header and a footer. On web it is rows on the page; on ios inset grouped cards of 52pt rows with section text above and below each card, or a flush list with hairlines from the text; on android 56dp rows with the section header as a small label.
useWhen: A short list of things people open: mail, files, boards, members
Rows that each carry one or two actions, such as delete or more
Ordered steps or a ranking, as an ol
Rows grouped under headings: settings groups, contacts by letter (ListSection, with SectionIndex for long lists)
Rows with quick actions behind a swipe, such as delete and archive on mail (ListItem swipe with SwipeActions)
Rows that do something in place, such as play a song (ListItem onSelect)
A settings row that is one control across the row, such as a volume slider (ListItem control)
Article rows with a title of up to three lines and their own buttons under the text (titleLines, ListItem footer)
avoidWhen: Picking one or more options from the rows
Many fields per row that people compare across rows
Term and value pairs about one thing
Site or app navigation with sections and nesting

size.description: md rows are at least list.row.height plus a small inset (about 36px in the default density), sm rows are list.row.height (28px default, 24 compact, 32 comfortable).

variant.description: plain: rows only. divided: a hairline between rows. inset: rows grouped on a rounded surface with hairlines. flush (order C1, proposed): full width rows with a hairline from the text edge, past the start part at its real size, to the row's inline end; no platform draws it as a card. Sets data-variant on the root.

ordered.description: Renders an ol for rows whose order means something.

titleLines.description: How many lines each row's title may wrap to before an ellipsis (order C1, proposed); all never cuts it. A row's own titleLines wins, and the rows of every ListSection take the list's. Above 1 the row stamps data-title-lines (2, 3 or all), grows downward, and start, end and actions line up with the first line, which sits where a one line row's would. Use all where a title must stay whole with larger text or text spacing (settings); a count cuts long titles with an ellipsis.

empty.description: Shown when there are no rows, in a p with part empty; the root is then a div. Say what is missing and what to do next. With aria-label the empty div takes role group.

ListItem.title.description: The row's main text, one line with an ellipsis unless titleLines allows more. With href it is the link, with onSelect the button. Optional in a control row.

ListItem.description.description: A second line, up to two lines then an ellipsis.

ListItem.start.description: A system icon name (hidden from assistive tech) or a node such as an Avatar.

ListItem.end.description: Trailing content that is not an action: a time, a count, a Badge, or the end glyph of a control row (an Icon). Positioned above the row link, so a link or Badge in it stays clickable.

ListItem.actions.description: Buttons or IconButtons for the row. Their own Tab stops, drawn above the row link.

ListItem.href.description: Makes the row a link: the title becomes an anchor whose hit area covers the row.

ListItem.onSelect.description: Makes the row act in place without going anywhere (play a song), order C1, proposed: the title becomes a span with role button and tabindex 0 whose hit area covers the row, and a click, Enter (key down) or Space (key up) runs it. The row stamps data-action and data-pressed while pressed, and draws no chevron. Ignored with href. Disabled keeps focus with aria-disabled and never runs.

ListItem.chevron.description: On a linked row, false asks the platform for no disclosure chevron and stamps data-no-chevron (order C1, proposed). Use it where the whole list goes to items of one kind, such as saved articles.

ListItem.titleLines.description: The row's own title line count; default the List's titleLines.

ListItem.control.description: One control that spans the row, such as a Slider, between the start and end glyphs (part control, order C1, proposed). title becomes optional and, when given, is drawn above the control across the row; description, footer, href and onSelect are not used. Name the control itself (aria-label).

ListItem.footer.description: The row's own buttons under its text, such as a listen capsule and a more button (part footer, order C1, proposed). Positioned above the row link like actions, their own Tab stops after the title. Name each with the row it acts on.

ListItem.linkProps.description: Extra anchor props: target, rel, onClick for a client router, aria-current.

ListItem.active.description: The current row. Sets data-active, the active fill, and aria-current (true, or the value in linkProps) on the link. The description and end step up to the default text color on the active fill.

ListItem.disabled.description: Dims the start icon and the title. A link loses its href, keeps focus with role link and aria-disabled (anatomy rule 5), and linkProps.onClick does not run. The description and end stay at full contrast, so the reason the row is off stays readable. Actions are the caller's to disable.

ListItem.swipe.description: Swipe actions for the row (order M9.7, proposed): a SwipeActions element with start, end, fullSwipe and menuLabel and no children. The row's own parts are what moves; the SwipeActions root becomes the row's last child, part swipe, an overlay holding the action groups and the menu button. Ignored on a disabled row.

ListSection.header.description: The section heading above its rows (part section-header, an h3 by default). It names the section's nested list and takes focus (tabindex -1) when a SectionIndex jumps to the section.

ListSection.footer.description: A note under the rows (part section-footer, a p): what the settings of the section do. It is the description of the section's nested list.

ListSection.level.description: The heading level of the header, 2 to 6, to fit the page outline.

ListSection.empty.description: Shown when the section has no rows, as in List.

ListSection.id.description: Put the id a SectionIndex targets here; the jump scrolls to the section and focuses its heading.

a11y.role: list (ul or ol) with listitem rows. A linked row's title is a link; an action row's title is a span with role button. An empty list is a div with a paragraph, so it is not read as a list of one. A list of sections is a ul with role group (named) or none (unnamed) holding li elements with role presentation; each holds a heading and a nested list named by it, so a reader says list, 4 items per section.
a11y.focus: Each linked or action row is one Tab stop on its title (link or button); its actions and then its footer buttons follow. A disabled row link or action stays focusable with aria-disabled. Rows without a link or an action and the list itself are not focusable. A 2px ring from color.focus.ring draws inside the whole row. A section heading is not a Tab stop; it takes focus (tabindex -1) when a SectionIndex jumps to it, with the same 2px ring.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next row link, row button, row action or footer button
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves to the previous row link, row button, row action or footer button
keys.Enter: Follows the focused row link, runs the focused action row (on key down), or activates the focused action
keys.Space: Runs the focused action row (on key up, as a native button), or activates the focused action button
keys.Shift+F10: On a row with swipe actions, opens the menu of those actions (SwipeActions)

a11y.announce: The link or button name is the title only; the description, end, actions and footer are read as the row's other content. Name each action and footer button with the row it acts on: Delete mail from Sara.
notes: No arrow key navigation: this is a list of links and buttons, not a composite widget. For arrow keys and selection use ListBox.
The row link's hit area is its ::before stretched over the row, which is also the focus layer. Actions are positioned later in the DOM, so they sit above it without a z-index.
Give the list an aria-label when the page has no heading for it.
Under forced colors the focus ring is Highlight, the active row gets a CanvasText outline and separators are CanvasText.
data-linked marks a row with a link, for CSS only; it is structure, not a state.
An active row without a link carries aria-current on the li.
ordered renders an ol for assistive tech; numbers are not drawn. Put a number in start when people need to see it.

Sections (order M9.2, proposed): the nested list of a section is its own List root with the outer size and variant, so an inset list draws one card per section and every row rule applies. The outer list of sections draws no fill and carries no data-variant. Rows and sections do not mix in one List.
Header and footer take the start edge and line up with the row text, so they align right in Arabic. The header is muted text at font.size.s (4.5:1); the footer the same at regular weight.

Swipe rows (order M9.7, proposed): the swipe part is a SwipeActions root and carries its states (data-state closed, open-start or open-end; data-dragging, data-armed, data-settling). The row clips, sets touch-action pan-y, and moves its parts by --_list-shift while the swipe is dragged, open or settling; once closed and settled no transform is left, so the row link covers the row again. The menu button of SwipeActions is the path that needs no drag; Shift+F10 in the row opens it.

Order C1 (proposed): data-action marks a row that acts in place, data-no-chevron a linked row with chevron false, data-title-lines (2, 3 or all) a row whose title may wrap. All for CSS only; structure, not states.

The action row's title is a span with role button, tabindex 0 and the keys of a native button (Enter on key down, Space on key up, no repeat), because the button gate allows no bare button outside Button and a system Button would make the title a part of Button. WCAG 2.2 2.1.1 and 4.1.2.

Wrapped titles (titleLines) keep the row's first line where a one line row puts it and grow the row downward, so at 320px wide a long title wraps instead of being cut (WCAG 2.2 1.4.10). With all the title is never cut, at 200 percent text or with text spacing (1.4.4, 1.4.12); with a count it ends with an ellipsis past that many lines, so a title cut there must be readable in full where the row leads.

A flush hairline is a grid item that starts at the title's column line, so it clears a start part of any size (a 64px cover); --_list-separator-inset moves it from there and --_list-separator-inset-end sets its distance from the row end (0, full bleed).

A control row (part control) lays out start, the control and end; it is never a link or an action. A footer (part footer) is a last grid row under the text with its own buttons, drawn above the row link.

en.title: A name people scan for: the sender, the file, the board. Sentence case.
en.description: One line of context: the subject, the last change.
en.empty: What is missing and what happens next: No mail yet. Mail you get from your team shows here.
en.actions: Accessible names say the verb and the row: Delete mail from Sara Alqahtani.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics.
ar.empty: ما فيه رسائل للحين. الرسائل اللي توصلك من فريقك بتظهر هنا.
ar.digits: Western digits in end content such as times and counts.
ar.description: سطر واحد يوضح السياق، بدون تشكيل.
ar.actions: Accessible names say the action and the row in noun form: حذف رسالة سارة القحطاني.

react.note: Hover and active swap the row fill at once. list-stagger (rows entering) is named for the catalog; the component plays no motion yet and leaves entry to the page.

native.note: FlatList rows with Pressable for linked rows; 44pt rows on iOS and 48dp on Android.

styles.web: Rows on the page; sections stack with the header above and the footer below each group.
styles.ios: Inset grouped cards with 52pt rows and a chevron on rows that go somewhere; the section header and footer sit outside the card in small muted text. flush is a full width list with hairlines from the text edge; an action row and a linked row with chevron false draw no chevron (the platform rules for flush, data-action and data-no-chevron are proposed in order C1).
styles.android: 56dp rows with a ripple from the touch point; the section header is a small label above its rows.
styles.studio: Flat rows, a 5 percent overlay on hover, a 10 percent overlay for the active row; inset groups on surface 2.
styles.desk: The same on the Desk tokens; inset groups read as a panel inside a window.
styles.neutral: The same on the Neutral tokens; no recipe.
styles.liquid: The same on the Liquid tokens; the card corner and hairline follow the platform on ios.

mistakes.wrong: A row with onClick on the li
mistakes.right: href on ListItem, so the row is a real link that keyboards and new tabs work with; onSelect when the row acts in place, such as play a song

mistakes.wrong: A List with checkboxes for picking rows
An action labelled Delete in every row
mistakes.right: Delete mail from Sara Alqahtani, so each name is unique

mistakes.wrong: An empty ul with nothing in it
mistakes.right: empty with what to do next

mistakes.wrong: A long sentence as the title, cut to one line with an ellipsis that a pointer user cannot read in full
mistakes.right: A short title of a few words, with the rest in description, which wraps to two lines

mistakes.wrong: A heading outside the List and a second List for each group
mistakes.right: ListSection with header and footer, so each group is a named list and a SectionIndex can jump to it

mistakes.wrong: ListItem rows and ListSection parts in one List
mistakes.right: Every row inside a ListSection once the list has sections

mistakes.wrong: A SwipeActions element wrapped around a ListItem
mistakes.right: ListItem swipe={<SwipeActions ... />}, so the row stays the list item and its parts stay the List's

mistakes.wrong: A linked row with a chevron for a tap that plays a song in place
mistakes.right: ListItem onSelect: a button row with no chevron

mistakes.wrong: A Slider passed as the title of a row
mistakes.right: ListItem control with start and end glyphs

mistakes.wrong: A long settings title cut to one line at 320px
mistakes.right: titleLines 2 or 3 on the List, so the title wraps and the row grows
